x: After the first half mile we had Masters, Walker and Bagnall in the first 20, with Patterson Baulch, Short, Trower and Bedford in the twenties, and although positions changed a bit, our scoring six were always placed well in the first thirty.
Short, Bagnall and Patterson, please oblige. It will be noted that the post-war boom in athletics shows itself in performances by club members.

Knight of Essex Beagles was the individual winner completing the course in record time and finishing in front of Sando. Pete Bagnall was our first man home in 11th position and supported by Masters, Short and L. Bishop, we gained 3rd place in the team event.
Half way round the first lap, Bagnall, Paterson, Short, Masters and Baulch were all between 20th and 30th in that order and Gebbett and Trower were in the next dozen.
He was accompanied over the first five miles by Pat Newell, followed by Walker, Bagnall, Short and Gebbett, but at this stage Short retired.
These four opened up a short gap from George Davidson. When the second lap of the Common was completed, Walker was again leading and Flanagan was beginning to feel the effects of the fast pace.
Then followed a string of runners before we again saw a Belgrave vest filled by Eddie Short who had John Moore and Jumbo Masters close on his heels, all of them in the 130's.

At the end of the first lap Clive Shippen was leading with Moore and Short well in attendance. A quick check showed that we were well in the lead and should have no difficulty in holding our position.
